Let \(a=BC,\ b=CA,\ c=AB\), and set \(x=\frac ba,\ y=\frac cb\). For the Brocard point \(P\),
\[
\frac{[PBC]}{[ABC]}=\frac{a^2c^2}{a^2b^2+b^2c^2+c^2a^2}.
\]
Also \(\triangle B_1CA\sim \triangle ABC\) with scale \(\frac ba\), and \(\triangle C_1AB\sim \triangle ABC\) with scale \(\frac cb\). Hence the area ratio is
\[
R=x^2+y^2+\frac{y^2}{1+y^2+x^2y^2}.
\]
Take an acute triangle with
\[
A=\varepsilon,\qquad B=C=\frac{\pi-\varepsilon}{2}.
\]
Then
\[
x=\frac{\sin B}{\sin A}=\frac{\cos(\varepsilon/2)}{\sin\varepsilon}\to\infty,\qquad y=1,
\]
so
\[
R=x^2+1+\frac{1}{x^2+2}\to\infty.
\]
Thus the area ratio is unbounded above, so no finite \(\lambda\) can satisfy the inequality for all acute triangles.

\[
\boxed{\text{No finite maximum}}
\]
